chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ishaq, from some of our companions, from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a mukatab (a slave who has contracted to pay a sum for his freedom) who became unable to pay the remainder, having already paid part of it.
He said: 'The remainder is paid on his behalf from the wealth of zakat (alms-tax).'
Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, says in His Book: 'And for the freeing of slaves.'

key_terms.الرِّقَابِ: Plural of 'raqabah', referring to slaves or captives, specifically in the context of freeing them.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his manumission.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The payment of the agreed sum for manumission.

ai.seo_question: How is the remaining freedom price paid for a slave who cannot afford it under Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a mukatab who becomes insolvent after partial payment is eligible for financial assistance from the zakat fund to complete their manumission. It explicitly links this legal mechanism to the Quranic category of 'fi al-riqab' (for freeing slaves), demonstrating the practical application of zakat in social emancipation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that zakat serves not only as charity for the poor but also as a tool for liberating those in servitude, reinforcing the spiritual and economic dimensions of freedom in Islamic law.
